question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=7y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=7$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{7t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, notice that:

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x$-axis. Since ${e}^{3t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{7t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $y$-axis. Since ${e}^{7t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

Among the given options, there are two phase portraits satisfying these conditions:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221064/assets/96801605aa5d777eb18c13ded1f7b7e59ae74968b210da3b7a26f339a1c9f673.png)

Let's consider the solutions $x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{3t}$ and $y(t)={c}_{2}{e}^{7t}$ provided that ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\ne 0.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}=\frac{({c}_{2}{e}^{7t})^{′}}{({c}_{1}{e}^{3t})^{′}}=\frac{7{c}_{2}{e}^{7t}}{3{c}_{1}{e}^{3t}}=\frac{7{c}_{2}}{3{c}_{1}}{e}^{4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\to \pm \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ meaning that the tangents to the solution become more and more vertical as we move away from the origin. This corresponds to the following phase portrait:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221064/assets/20ef7519d0ca517d0d7d06d2998f7bd6c77f04145243f721e197fbef5c087791.png)
